key_insight: The paper reframes stellar convection as a phase-space density of fluid particles, deriving mean-field equations from Liouvillian dynamics and using phase-space divergence as a local stability diagnostic.
engineering_relevance: This provides a physically grounded alternative to prescribed mixing-length closures for modeling convection near surfaces and convective boundaries in stellar evolution codes.
method: Represent the flow as a distribution over position-velocity phase space.
Derive Reynolds-Favre mean-field equations as velocity-space moments of a conservation law.
Use the Liouvillian formulation to interpret phase-space divergence (\{s,T\}) as local contraction/expansion and stability; extendable to rotation, magnetic fields, and composition effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical derivation and qualitative stability interpretation, but does not report numerical experiments or quantitative benchmark data.
watch_item: The approach is formally elegant but may be difficult to implement robustly in realistic stellar models because it requires phase-space-resolved closures and careful treatment of non-adiabatic regions.
paper_title: Phase-space averaging for stellar convection I. Liouvillian dynamics
